definition: The belief that one is inherently deserving of privileges or special treatment
etymology: From Old French 'entitler' (to give a title to), from Latin 'intitulare'
contextSentence: Do not fall into the trap, the entitlement trap, a feeling like you're a victim.
contextSentenceKo: 함정에 빠지지 마세요. 특권 의식이라는 함정, 자신이 피해자라는 느낌 말이에요.

definition: To put something or someone into a situation in which there is a danger of loss, harm, or failure
etymology: From Old French 'jeu parti' (divided game, uncertain outcome)
contextSentence: Whatever your answer is, don't choose anything that will jeopardize yourself.
contextSentenceKo: 답이 무엇이든, 자신을 위태롭게 하는 것은 선택하지 마세요.

definition: To cause someone to become hostile; to act in opposition to something
contextSentence: Don't spend time with anything that antagonizes your character.
contextSentenceKo: 당신의 인격에 반하는 것에 시간을 쓰지 마세요.

definition: To designate or treat something as more important than other things
contextSentence: Prioritize who you are, who you want to be.
contextSentenceKo: 당신이 누구인지, 누가 되고 싶은지 우선순위를 정하세요.

definition: The process of removing or getting rid of something; the act of excluding possibilities
etymology: From Latin 'eliminare' (to turn out of doors, expel)
contextSentence: I know who I am not. Process of elimination.
contextSentenceKo: 나는 내가 누구가 아닌지 안다. 소거법이다.

definition: To engage in casual or unconstrained conversation about other people, typically involving unverified details
etymology: From Old English 'godsibb' (godparent), later shifting to mean a close friend who shares secrets
rootBreakdown: god (God) + sibb (related, kin) → evolved to mean idle talk
contextSentence: You know they gossip too much or they're kind of shady.
contextSentenceKo: 험담을 너무 많이 하거나 약간 수상한 사람들이죠.

definition: Of doubtful honesty or legality; suspicious (informal)
etymology: From 'shade' (shadow, darkness) + -y, metaphor for hiding in shadows
contextSentence: They're kind of shady, they really aren't gonna be there for you in a pinch.
contextSentenceKo: 약간 수상한 사람들이죠. 정작 어려울 때 곁에 있어주지 않을 거예요.

definition: A severe headache or other after-effects caused by drinking an excess of alcohol
etymology: From 'hang over' (to remain from a previous time), 19th century
contextSentence: That bar that we keep going to that we always seem to have the worst hangover from.
contextSentenceKo: 갈 때마다 항상 최악의 숙취에 시달리는 그 술집.

definition: Affected by lethargy; sluggish and apathetic
contextSentence: We feel lethargic, we keep putting on weight.

definition: Without intention; accidentally; as an unintended consequence
etymology: From Latin 'inadvertens' (not turning the mind to)
contextSentence: You inadvertently find yourself spending more time in more places that are healthy for you.
contextSentenceKo: 자연스럽게 건강에 좋은 곳에서 더 많은 시간을 보내게 됩니다.

definition: A cruel and oppressive ruler; a person exercising power in a cruel or arbitrary way
contextSentence: Too many options will make a tyrant of us all.
contextSentenceKo: 너무 많은 선택지는 우리 모두를 폭군으로 만듭니다.

definition: An amount of something that is more than necessary, permitted, or desirable
contextSentence: Get rid of the excess, the wasted time, decrease your options.
contextSentenceKo: 불필요한 것을 없애세요. 낭비되는 시간을. 선택지를 줄이세요.

definition: Having or showing good judgment; able to judge quality and make careful distinctions
contextSentence: Be discerning. Choose it because you want it.

definition: Reparation or compensation for a loss or injury; typically used in 'make amends'
etymology: From Old French 'amendes' (penalties, fines), from Latin 'emendare' (to correct)
contextSentence: You got to own them, then you got to make amends.

definition: A feeling of sadness, repentance, or disappointment over something that has happened or been done
etymology: From Old French 'regreter' (to bewail, lament the dead)
contextSentence: Guilt and regret kills many a man before their time.
contextSentenceKo: 죄책감과 후회는 제때가 되기도 전에 많은 사람을 죽입니다.

definition: A person who designs buildings; (figurative) a person who is responsible for creating or shaping something
contextSentence: Since we are the architects of our own lives, let's study the habits.
contextSentenceKo: 우리가 자신의 삶의 건축가이니까, 습관을 연구합시다.

definition: To methodically cut up for detailed examination; to analyze something in minute detail
etymology: From Latin 'dissectus', past participle of 'dissecare' (to cut apart)
contextSentence: Let's dissect that and give thanks for those things.

definition: A current score or amount; a record of points or items
etymology: From Anglo-Latin 'tallia' (tax, a cutting), from Latin 'talea' (a stick, rod)
rootBreakdown: tally (from Latin talea: a notched stick for counting)
contextSentence: Take that daily tally, tend our garden.
